title: Introduction to Cosmos DB
description: Discover Cosmos DB as a globally distributed, multi-model database that supports document, key-value, graph, and column-family data models.

data.text: Azure Cosmos DB is a fully managed NoSQL database designed for global distribution and low latency at any scale. Unlike traditional databases that require you to choose between consistency and performance, Cosmos DB offers five distinct consistency levels that you can tune per request. It also supports multiple data APIs, so you can work with document, key-value, graph, or column-family data without switching database platforms.

data.title: Global by Default
data.text: Cosmos DB replicates your data across any number of Azure regions with a single click. You can configure your application to read from the nearest region to users, achieving single-digit-millisecond latency around the world.

Cosmos DB exposes several data APIs so you can use the query language and SDKs that best fit your application. The same underlying database engine powers all APIs, so you can mix and match APIs for different microservices or change APIs without migrating data.

data.title: Supported Data APIs
items: NoSQL: native JSON document storage with SQL-like querying.
MongoDB: wire-compatible with the MongoDB API for existing MongoDB applications.
Cassandra: column-family API for wide-column workloads.
Gremlin: graph database API for connected data and relationship queries.
Table: key-value API compatible with Azure Table Storage.

data.text: Cosmos DB lets you choose the consistency guarantee that fits your application needs. The five levels form a spectrum from strongest to weakest guarantees, and stronger consistency typically means slightly higher latency because more replicas must confirm the write before it is acknowledged.

cards.title: Strong
cards.description: Linearizable consistency. Reads are guaranteed to return the most recent committed version of an item.

cards.title: Bounded Staleness
cards.description: Reads may lag behind writes by a fixed number of versions or time interval.
cons: Requires careful version and time tuning

cards.title: Session
cards.description: Monotonic reads and writes within a client session. This is the most commonly used level.
pros: Best balance of latency and consistency
Guarantees no writes are lost within a session
cons: Different sessions may see different versions

cards.title: Consistent Prefix
cards.description: Reads never see out-of-order writes, but may return older versions.

cards.title: Eventual
cards.description: Replicas eventually converge. Reads may return older data temporarily.

data.text: Every Cosmos DB container is partitioned by a partition key you choose at creation time. Cosmos DB distributes items across physical partitions based on the hash value of the partition key. A good partition key has many distinct values and distributes requests evenly so no single partition becomes a hotspot.

data.title: Choosing a Partition Key
data.text: Choose a partition key that has many distinct values and is frequently used in your WHERE clause or query filter. Avoid keys with few values or that create hot partitions, such as timestamps that concentrate writes at the current time.

Cosmos DB does not use traditional CPU or memory metrics. Instead, it abstracts resources into Request Units (RU) per second. A single RU represents the resources needed to read a 1 KB item. More complex operations like queries with joins or writes consume more RUs. You provision throughput at the container or database level in increments of RUs per second.

data.title: Create a Cosmos DB Container with Azure CLI
data.content: Creates a SQL API container with 400 RU/s throughput and /category as the partition key.
data.code:
az cosmosdb sql database create \
  --account-name myCosmosAccount \
  --resource-group myResourceGroup \
  --name myDatabase

az cosmosdb sql container create \
  --account-name myCosmosAccount \
  --resource-group myResourceGroup \
  --database-name myDatabase \
  --name myContainer \
  --partition-key-path "/category" \
  --throughput 400

terms.definition: A guarantee about how quickly read operations return the latest committed write across replicated regions.
A property chosen at container creation that determines how items are distributed across physical partitions.
A normalized measure of the resources required to perform a database operation in Cosmos DB.
The fundamental unit of scalability in Cosmos DB, equivalent to a table in relational databases or a collection in document databases.

data.title: Design a Partition Key
data.description: You are building a retail application with orders. Each order has an orderId, customerId, orderDate, and region. Choose a partition key and explain your reasoning.
steps: Evaluate whether orderId, customerId, or region would distribute writes evenly.
Consider which key is most frequently used in your queries.
Avoid keys with low cardinality or that concentrate recent activity.
Document your chosen partition key and the trade-offs you considered.
data.expectedOutcome: You can explain how partition key choice affects Cosmos DB performance and cost, and justify a partition key for a given workload.

data.title: Cosmos DB Essentials
points: Cosmos DB is a globally distributed, multi-model NoSQL database.
It supports NoSQL, MongoDB, Cassandra, Gremlin, and Table APIs.
Five consistency levels let you tune latency versus freshness.
Partitioning distributes data across physical partitions using a partition key.
Throughput is measured in Request Units (RU) per second.
data.takeaway: Cosmos DB gives you worldwide low-latency access to data with the flexibility to choose the data model, API, and consistency level that matches your application requirements.
